title: ChromeOS: register a Chromebox with Google CDM and assign your kiosk app
summary: Enrol a Chromebox in Google Chrome Device Management, add the kiosk app in the Google Admin console and set it to auto-launch at start-up.
bodyMd:
A Chromebox becomes a managed digital-signage device once it is enrolled in Google Chrome Device Management (CDM) and set to auto-launch a kiosk app. This article covers the enrolment and the kiosk settings in the Google Admin console. Allow about 20 minutes per device, less once the organisational unit settings are in place.

Before you begin

  • The Chromebox powered on and connected to the internet.
  • A Google Workspace account with super admin access.
  • An organisational unit for your displays — see ChromeOS: set up a new organisational unit in Google CDM.
  • The kiosk player's app URL and companion extension details for your organisation.

Enrol the Chromebox in Chrome Device Management

  1. Turn on the Chromebox.
  2. Follow the on-screen prompts until the sign-in screen appears. Do not sign in.
  3. Press Ctrl + Alt + E to open the enrolment screen.
  4. Enter your Google Workspace username and password.
  5. Select Enroll device.

    The device registers with Chrome Device Management and shows a confirmation.

  6. On the sign-in screen that follows, sign in with your Google Workspace account.

Add the kiosk app

The Personalisation Hub kiosk player runs as a Progressive Web App (PWA), so it is added by URL rather than by searching the Chrome Web Store — this and the companion extension in the next step are the 2 parts of this setup that are easiest to miss.

  1. Sign in to the Google Admin console with your administrator account.
  2. Go to Devices → Chrome Devices.
  3. Select the Chromebox, then select Device settings.
  4. Choose the organisational unit the settings apply to — the top-level unit or the child unit that holds your displays.
  5. Scroll to Kiosk Settings and select Manage Kiosk Applications.
  6. In the Kiosk Applications panel, select Add kiosk application → Progressive Web App, then enter the kiosk player's app URL.
  7. Select Add, then Save.

Add the companion extension

The kiosk PWA needs a companion extension added alongside it, configured with a JSON manifest — without it the app loads but cannot reach the device features the player needs (for example camera access for QR Control).

  1. In the same Kiosk Applications panel, select Add kiosk application → Chrome app or extension.
  2. Enter the companion extension's ID and update URL, or paste its JSON configuration if you were given one.
  3. Select Add, then Save.

Set the kiosk app to auto-launch

  1. Return to Device settings for the same organisational unit.
  2. Scroll to Kiosk Settings and, in Auto-Launch Kiosk App, select the PWA you added.
  3. Select Save.
Keep the device powered on and connected to the internet while the settings apply. Changes made while a device is offline take effect after its next restart.

Verify it worked

Restart the Chromebox. It starts straight into the kiosk app without showing the sign-in screen. When the app connects to your platform domain, it shows a Register this display screen with a registration code — continue with Register a new display or device.

Troubleshooting

The kiosk app does not launch after restart

Cause. The device was offline when you saved the settings, or the device sits in a different organisational unit from the one you configured.

Fix. Connect the device to the internet and restart it. In Devices → Chrome Devices, confirm which organisational unit the device belongs to.
